paper_metadata.title: Exceptional strength-ductility synergy at room and liquid nitrogen temperatures of Al7.5Co20.5Fe24Ni24Cr24 high-entropy alloy with hierarchical precipitate heterogeneous structure

evidence.quote: The current investigation delves into the impact of diverse thermo-mechanical treatments on the phase and microstructure evolution in a face-centered cubic (FCC) Al7.5Co20.5Fe24Ni24Cr24 HEA.

For the CRSA sample, a distinct single-phase equiaxed microstructure with uniform grain orientation was observed (Fig. 3(a1)-(a2)). The average grain size was measured to be 35.5 μm.

In contrast, the CRRA sample exhibited a heterogeneous grain structure after undergoing high-temperature short-term heat treatment at 1100 ◦C for 20 s (Fig. 3(c1)-(c3)). This structure comprises two distinct types of regions, i.e., coarse recrystallized grain (CRG) regions measuring ~18.3 μm and ultra-fine grain (UFG) regions measuring ~1.4 μm.
Following aging at 700 ℃ for 2 h, CRRA700 inherited the heterogeneous grain structure from CRRA, consisting of CRG measuring ~19.4 μm and UFG measuring ~1.4 μm (Fig. 3(d1)-(d3)).

It can be clearly seen from the inverse pole figure (IPF) and grain orientation spread (GOS) maps that the sample possessed a partially recrystallized structure (Fig. 4(a) and (b)). The recrystallized and non-recrystallized zone are highlighted in green and white in the GOS map, respectively (Fig. 4(b)). The volume fractions of recrystallized and non-recrystallized regions are measured to be ~52.9 vol.% and ~47.1 vol.%, respectively. The recrystallized grains have an average size of ~0.86 μm
